terminology.custody: Joint Legal Custody / Joint Physical Custody

residencyRequirements.description: At least one spouse must have been a resident of the State of Nevada for at least six (6) weeks immediately preceding the filing of the complaint. Residency is corroborated by a Resident Witness Affidavit (NRS 125.123; court practice).

waitingPeriod.description: Nevada has NO mandatory waiting period after filing. The divorce can be finalized as soon as all papers are processed and any required hearing is held.

noFault.name: Living Separate and Apart for One Year
noFault.description: The parties have lived separate and apart for one year without cohabitation

fault.name: Insanity
fault.description: Insanity existing for two (2) years prior to the filing of the complaint, supported by medical evidence

groundsForDissolution.notes: Nevada is primarily a no-fault state. 'Incompatibility' is by far the most common ground. The insanity ground requires medical evidence and is rarely used.

propertyDivision.description: Nevada is a community property state. Community property is divided equally (50/50) between the spouses. The court may make an unequal disposition only upon a finding of a compelling reason set forth in writing. Separate property (property acquired before the marriage, by gift, or by inheritance) remains with the owning spouse.
propertyDivision.separateProperty: Property acquired before marriage, by gift, or by inheritance is separate property and remains with the owning spouse. Commingling separate property with community property may convert it to community property.

legalCitations.description: Residency requirement — 6 weeks state residency (corroborating affidavit per NRS 125.123)
Grounds for divorce — incompatibility, 1-year separation, insanity
Community property — equal 50/50 division; unequal only with compelling reason in writing
Alimony — court may award alimony to either party
Joint legal custody (NRS 125C.002) and joint physical custody (NRS 125C.0025)
Best interest of the child standard for custody determination
Nevada Child Support Guidelines (eff. Feb 1, 2020, adopted under NRS 425.620) — tiered percentages of the obligor's gross monthly income

filingFees.notes: Filing fees vary by county. Clark County (Las Vegas) charges approximately $364 for a Complaint for Divorce. Washoe County (Reno) charges approximately $284-$326. Rural counties vary. Fee waivers (Application to Proceed In Forma Pauperis) are available for qualifying low-income individuals.

basic.name: Complaint for Divorce
basic.description: Initiates the divorce proceeding (Nevada uses 'Complaint' rather than 'Petition')

basic.name: Resident Witness Affidavit
basic.description: Affidavit from a third-party witness confirming the plaintiff has resided in Nevada for at least 6 weeks (NRS 125.020)

basic.name: Financial Disclosure Form
basic.description: Disclosure of income, assets, and debts

basic.name: Decree of Divorce
basic.description: Final court order dissolving the marriage

service.name: Summons
service.description: Formal service on defendant via sheriff, process server, or certified mail

service.name: Waiver of Service / Acceptance of Service
service.description: Defendant voluntarily accepts service and waives formal process
service.notes: Must be signed by defendant and filed with the court

withChildren.name: Custody/Visitation Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing joint legal custody, physical custody, and visitation schedule per NRS 125C

withChildren.name: Child Support Worksheet
withChildren.description: Calculation per the Nevada Child Support Guidelines (NAC 425.140 et seq.)

withChildren.name: Child Support Order
withChildren.description: Court order establishing child support obligations

formattingRequirements.notes: Per Nevada Rules of Civil Procedure

inState.description: Defendant must file an answer within 21 days of service within Nevada

outOfState.description: Defendant served outside Nevada must file an answer within 21 days of service (additional time may be granted)

childSupportGuidelines.description: Nevada uses tiered percentages of the obligor's gross monthly income under NAC 425.140 (eff. Feb 1, 2020): for one child, 16% of the first $6,000, 8% of the next $4,000, and 4% above $10,000; two children 22%/11%/6%, with higher tiers for more children. The court may deviate based on the best interest of the child.
childSupportGuidelines.notes: The guideline percentages serve as a presumptive amount. The court may adjust based on factors including the cost of health insurance, child care, and special needs.

maintenanceGuidelines.description: Nevada courts may award alimony to either party. There is no fixed formula. The court considers the financial condition of each spouse, the nature and value of their respective property, each party's contribution to the marriage (including homemaking), the duration of the marriage, each party's income, earning capacity, age, and health, and the standard of living during the marriage.
maintenanceGuidelines.eligibility: Available to either spouse. Generally more likely in longer marriages. No statutory formula — courts have broad discretion.

court.name: Family Court or District Court
court.description: Divorce is filed in Family Court in counties that have one (Clark County, Washoe County) or in the District Court in rural counties. (NRS 3.223)
